newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply weighs down prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply weighs down prices.

text.p: A flood of new issues clipped U.S. municipal bonds by 1/4 to 1/2 of a point on Thursday, leaving traders fretting that yields might have to rise 10 to 15 basis points for the market to absorb next week's sales.

Issuers plan to sell at least $4 billion of municipal bonds next week, while at the short-end of the yield curve, the California Regents System expects to sell a total of $660 million of commercial paper in two deals.

Retail investors this week bought notes with maturities of up to seven years and institutional players snapped up long-term bonds, but little interest was seen in the intermediate sector, called "the belly."
As a result, some of the intermediate bonds in at least one of the deals sold on Wednesday have been discounted.
"The 10-year part of the curve is trading down 10 basis points," a trader said.

In another sign of weaker prices for intermediate issues, on Thursday the calculation of the yield on the Reuters 10-year index of general obligation bonds rose three basis points to 5.06 percent from last Thursday. As has been the case for several months, dealers appeared unwilling to hold onto inventory for long, in part due to fears that next week's offerings will prove more attractive. "The market has a very short attention span right now. If you're not done in the primary market, basically you have 48 hours," a trader said.
Yet activity in the secondary market, which saw considerable selling pressure on Wednesday when an estimated $300 million of bid wanted lists circulating, died down on Thursday, traders said.
Because major players like mutual funds have not attracted large supplies of new cash, most business is being done on a swap basis, which complicates trading.
"Fund cash flows have been flat for the year, which really keeps a lid on trading," a trader said.

While dealers appeared to be concentrating on cleaning their shelves of intermediate issues, the market also was looking to economic data that will be released on Friday and next week, which should help set the overall direction.

The often volatile durable goods report for September, which is due out on Friday at 0830 EDT, is expected to show a two percent rise, according to a Reuters consensus poll of economists. And the economic calender for next week includes the Employment Cost Index on Monday, the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index on Wednesday, and the payrolls report on Friday.
"The market could get bailed out by a little better tone," a trader said. "But if it gets ugly, it could get real ugly," he added.

The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell 20 ticks to 113-31/32, again underperforming the December U.S. Treasury bond futures, which shed eight ticks to 110-19/32.
The MOB spread was little changed at plus 108 ticks.

In the secondary market, actively traded issues included Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Throughway Revenues, which have a five percent coupon. The issues were bid at 5.77 percent, NET, unchanged.
And Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2013, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.82 percent, NET, up three basis points.
